_releases.body:
Upgrade with `pip install -U pocketvina`.

### New
- `pair.export(protein=True)` writes the protein next to the poses, and
  `pair.export(ligand=False, protein=True)` writes only the protein.
  `pair.export_protein()` still works.
- `atlas.download()` copies the Atlas data licence (`LICENSE`) into the folder.

### Changes
- The PocketVina Atlas is faster over the internet, especially from far away
  (e.g. Colab): `select()` and `show()` of the docs example take about 2 s
  instead of 9 s.
- `show(theme="dark")` is dark from the start.
- Output says "highest-affinity pose" and "lowest Vina score" instead of
  "best", as on the Atlas website. `pocketvina dock` and `pocketvina info`
  now print "highest-affinity poses: ..."; `pocketvina info --json` is
  unchanged.
- Export paths: a path without an extension, or ending in "/", is a folder
  (created if needed). A file with the wrong extension, e.g. `abl1.pdb` for
  SDF poses, is an error, and nothing is written.
- Docs: the [Atlas page](https://bioinformatics.mdc-berlin.de/PocketVina/atlas.html)
  shows each step with its real output, and the other guides show code one
  step at a time. Links go to the Atlas website's new address,
  https://pocketvina-atlas.mdc-berlin.de/.

Full list in the [changelog](https://bioinformatics.mdc-berlin.de/PocketVina/changelog.html).

_releases.body:
Orphos 0.5.0 makes single-genome prediction about twice as fast and metagenomic prediction of short contigs about 16x faster, holds a tenth of the memory on inputs of many sequences, numbers the sequences of an input as Prodigal does, and matches Prodigal's master branch line for line on multi-sequence metagenomic input. Library users: `OrphosResults::training_used` is now an `Arc<Training>` and `SequenceInfo` has a new `number` field.


### Added

- `OrphosAnalyzer::analyze_sequences` analyzes the records of one input in
  order, numbering them; `analyze_fasta_file` and the Python and
  WebAssembly bindings go through it.
- `OrphosAnalyzer::analyze_numbered_sequence` analyzes one sequence under a
  given number, for callers that read an input one sequence at a time.
- `SequenceInfo::number`, the number of a sequence in its input, counted
  from 1. Code that builds a `SequenceInfo` has to set it.
- `output::write_all_results` writes the results of the sequences of one
  input as one output; the command line and the bindings use it.

### Fixed

- The sequences of a multi-sequence input are numbered as Prodigal numbers
  them. Every sequence used to be number 1, so the genes of every sequence
  were `1_1`, `1_2`, ... and every GFF sequence header said `seqnum=1`; the
  first gene of the second sequence is now `2_1` and its header `seqnum=2`.
  This shows in GFF output and in the name column of BED output. Output for
  a single sequence is unchanged.
- GFF output of several sequences has one `##gff-version` line, at the top,
  instead of one per sequence (`write_all_results`; `write_results` still
  writes one sequence as a complete output).
- A sequence of one or two bases no longer hangs node creation when ends
  are open, as they are by default.
- With `-m`, a run of `N` that lasts to the end of a sequence is not masked,
  as in Prodigal, which records a run when it reads the base after it;
  genes reaching into such a run were dropped.
- A start codon of the reverse strand within twenty bases of the end of the
  sequence is given the Shine-Dalgarno motifs Prodigal finds for it;
  Prodigal also searches from positions past the end there, and such a
  search can find a motif that no other does.
- In metagenomic mode a sequence in which no preset model finds a gene is
  reported under the first model tried for its GC content, as in Prodigal,
  instead of under model 0.
- Tests compare the GFF output with files written by a build of Prodigal's
  master branch, line by line, for inputs of many short sequences, runs of
  `N`, closed ends, masking and translation table 4
  (`tests/prodigal_reference_outputs.rs`).

### Changed

- **Breaking:** `OrphosResults::training_used` is an `Arc<Training>`
  instead of a `Training`. A model is half a megabyte and every result held
  its own copy, so 400 contigs held 250 MB and a large metagenome could not
  fit in memory; in metagenomic mode the results of a preset now share its
  model (24 MB for the same 400 contigs). Reading the model is unchanged;
  code that builds an `OrphosResults` wraps the model in an `Arc`, and code
  that changes it goes through `Arc::make_mut`.
  `metagenomic::get_preset_training_shared` returns a preset's shared model.
- Metagenomic mode no longer rebuilds the Shine-Dalgarno motif table for
  every preset model of every sequence; the table depends on the model
  alone and is now built once per model, from the 64 patterns of matching
  bases instead of the 4096 6-mers. The same holds for the gene length
  factors of a model and the codon table of a genetic code, and the motifs
  upstream of the start codons are read once per sequence rather than once
  per model. A metagenome of 400 contigs of 1 to 8 kb is predicted in 0.29 s
  instead of 4.9 s on one thread, and in 0.05 s instead of 0.63 s on ten.
- In metagenomic mode the preset models of a long sequence are scored on
  several threads, each on its own copy of the nodes, with at most 256 MB of
  copies at a time over all sequences: *E. coli* K-12 takes 0.55 s instead
  of 2.2 s on ten threads, and 530 MB instead of 245 MB. Sequences of fewer
  than 4096 nodes, and runs on one thread, are scored as before.
- Single-genome prediction is about twice as fast, on one thread and on
  many (*E. coli* K-12: 0.22 s instead of 0.39 s on one thread, 0.15 s
  instead of 0.29 s on ten), and uses less memory. The dynamic programming
  visits only the sources that can connect to a target: the latest ones for
  the connections that reach back a bounded distance, the reverse stops
  whose open reading frame is still open, and for the 3'-to-3' connections
  across strands the few sources that can overlap a gene, the rest being
  resolved by a sliding-window maximum. Node positions are created and
  sorted on their own, and every node is then written once; the strand
  scans visit only start and stop codons; the raw coding scores computed
  for training are kept for the prediction instead of being computed
  twice; the GC frame plot is kept as running totals per codon, so the GC
  bias of a node is a subtraction instead of a walk over its codons; the
  ORF GC content counts bases 32 at a time; and the coding score reads one
  codon per step and remembers the length factor of each gene length.
- Start training without Shine-Dalgarno motifs is about three times as
  fast, so that *M. genitalium* is predicted in 0.047 s instead of 0.11 s:
  it searched the motifs of every start node twice per iteration, and now
  once, on compact copies of the nodes and of the sequence windows the
  searches read.
- None of the above changes the output.
- Gene prediction on a single genome reuses the nodes training created and
  sorted, with their scores reset, instead of creating and sorting them a
  second time; nodes are sorted in place instead of being gathered into a
  second array; the node vector is sized from the sequence length; and
  sequences are encoded with the vector encoder when runs of `N` are masked
  too. The nodes of the two strands are created on two threads while the
  GC frame plot is computed on a third, and the three passes of the raw
  coding score, the GC bias record, the ORF GC content and the scans of the
  Shine-Dalgarno start training run per strand on two threads, each strand
  through its own view of the shared nodes so that nothing is copied or
  written back. On a pool of one thread the same passes run in place on the
  calling thread, as fast as before or faster. Output is unchanged; E. coli
  K-12 is predicted in about 0.6 s instead of 0.9 s on four cores.


## What's Changed
* Reuse training nodes, cut allocations, and run per-strand passes on two threads by @Ffloriel in https://github.com/FullHuman/orphos/pull/12
* Speed up prediction, number sequences, and match Prodigal on multi-sequence input by @Ffloriel in https://github.com/FullHuman/orphos/pull/13
* chore: prepare release 0.5.0 by @Ffloriel in https://github.com/FullHuman/orphos/pull/14


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/FullHuman/orphos/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0

_releases.body:
## Apple Silicon support

Run ESMFold2 binder design and the final critic on Apple Silicon through PyTorch/MPS. Download and extract the source archive below, then run the following from its top-level directory in a native arm64 terminal with Git and uv installed.

```bash
./install-macos.sh
source "$HOME/esmfold2-mac/env.sh"
esmfold2-pipeline launch example_configs/apple/pdl1-vhh.yaml --esm-repo "$ESM_REPO"
```

For optional Protenix V2 validation on Metal, add `--protenix-data /path/to/protenix-data` to the installer command. Supply the V2 checkpoint at `checkpoint/protenix-v2.pt` inside that directory. [Apple Silicon guide](https://github.com/cytokineking/esmfold2-pipeline/blob/v1.1.0/guide/apple-silicon.md)

## Other changes since v1.0.1

- Rank designs using ESMFold2 and validator confidence together with binder pose agreement after target alignment.
- Score the binder–target interface using native Protenix expected-TM data and export validation diagnostics.
- Preserve target sequences when resuming planned campaigns and use the prepared sequences for validation.

## Verification

The 150-step PD-L1/VHH design and final critic completed in 22 min 22 s on a 128 GB M5 Max. On an NVIDIA A100 80 GB, the Linux installer built fresh CUDA 12.8 environments and a two-step design completed through template-enabled Protenix V2 validation and ranking. The CUDA suite passed all 411 tests. [Port verification](https://github.com/cytokineking/esmfold2-pipeline/pull/4)

The source archive includes both platform installers and the example inputs. The wheel contains the Python package. Verify either download against the attached SHA256SUMS.

## [0.30.1] - 2026-11-11

### Fixed
- **An RFD3 contig that starts with a designed segment now builds one chain.** In a contig such as
  `12-20,C33-59,18-28` the leading designed run came back as a separate chain, 11-13 A from the motif with no
  peptide bond. It now joins the motif's chain, as a comma means; contigs that start with the motif are unchanged.
- **Release wheels are built with a hash-locked toolchain**, so the wheel on PyPI no longer depends on whichever
  `build`, `twine` and `setuptools` PyPI served on release day. The package contents are unchanged.
_releases.name: v0.30.1

_releases.body:
## [0.30.0] - 2026-11-09

### Changed
- **tt-bio no longer opens a network listener during a fold.** tt-metal's bundled OpenMPI listened on every interface
  for the whole run; tt-bio now defaults `OMPI_MCA_btl=^tcp`, since one host needs only `self` and `sm`.
  A value you set yourself wins; set it if you run tt-metal across hosts. Outputs are unchanged.
- **BoltzGen designs start each stage faster.** The featurizer process is spawned without waiting on its imports and
  one imported spare is kept ahead, removing ~3 s of serial wait per stage, and the refold's confidence heads run
  on the device with the per-sample pair terms built once. Same results.
_releases.name: v0.30.0

_releases.body:
## [0.29.0] - 2026-11-08

### Added
- **BindCraft 2 on the benchmarks page.** 352 s per 140-iteration design trajectory against PD-L1 on one Blackhole
  p150a, against 44.4 s on a B200, 52.0 s on an H200 and 119 s on an A100, each NVIDIA card on BindCraft 2's fastest
  shipped option. A Galaxy Blackhole delivers 1.8x a DGX B200's designs per dollar of purchase price.
_releases.name: v0.29.0

_releases.body:
## [0.28.0] - 2026-11-07

### Added
- **A PPI grade says when it could not score the binder's pose.** The two binder-pose RMSDs under
  `ppi_refolding` align on the target's absolute conditioned coordinates, so a design whose target was pinned with
  `C_CRDGRP` (an internal coordinate group, RFD4's recommended binder recipe) has nothing to align on and the `ppi`
  criterion comes back `pass = 0` with `all_metrics_present = 0`. That is upstream's behaviour and it reads exactly
  like a design that was scored and failed. `tt-bio evaluate` now names those designs and the columns it could not
  compute, and `docs/rfd4-design.md` says which conditioning to use if you intend to grade a binder's pose.
### Fixed
- **An RFD4 grade scores the designed chain again.** Every metric defined on the chain of interest
  (`refolded_target_aligned_binder_rmsd`, `refolded_target_backbone_aligned_binder_rmsd`) was computed over an
  empty atom subset, because the evaluate path matched the oracle's chain label against a chain instance id it
  synthesised itself: `B_1` against the `B` the oracle wrote. The subset is no longer empty, and a confidence JSON
  written with either spelling now resolves to the same chain. A refold also inherits its design's `C_CRD` and
  `SA_CRDSRC` masks, which an oracle's plain output structure does not carry, so metrics aligned on them are
  scored rather than dropped.
_releases.name: v0.28.0

_releases.body:
## [0.27.1] - 2026-11-07

### Fixed
- **OpenDDE and ESMFold2 no longer hang Wormhole chips.** On Wormhole, OpenDDE (normal and `--fast`) and ESMFold2
  `--fast` ran the trunk's matmuls at HiFi2. Under sustained load one core of such a matmul could stall and the chip
  stopped answering: on two JapanFold Galaxies this hit about 8-11 % of OpenDDE antibody-antigen targets. The
  Wormhole trunk runs at HiFi3 again, the fidelity it used before 0.21.0; Blackhole is unchanged. HiFi3 is the more
  precise setting and costs OpenDDE about 2 % at 608 tokens on Wormhole.
_releases.name: v0.27.1

_releases.body:
## [0.27.0] - 2026-11-06

### Added
- **RFD4-Proteina on the benchmarks page.** 3.74 s per design on one Blackhole p150a at batch 40, against 1.12 s on
  a B200, 1.48 s on an H200 and 3.50 s on an A100, each NVIDIA card at its own best batch. A Galaxy Blackhole
  delivers 4.2x a DGX B200's designs per dollar of purchase price.
- **Mol-1 (`--model mol1`).** Molence Bio's Protenix-derived structure model folds protein, DNA, RNA, ligand and ion
  complexes on the Protenix engine. It reads upstream's job-list JSON unchanged, writes upstream's per-seed output
  layout with its summary and full-data confidence files, and defaults to upstream's 20 recycles, 200 steps and 5
  samples. For Protenix and Mol-1 job JSON, `--use_seeds_in_json` runs every seed in a job's
  `modelSeeds` instead of `--seed`, one result per seed. The weights download on first use; Molence has not stated a
  licence for them yet. On a Wormhole Galaxy chip it takes up to 1024 tokens and refuses larger inputs before
  opening a device. See `docs/mol1.md`.
- Mol-1's mmCIF now carries upstream's `_entry`, `_chem_comp`, `_entity`, `_entity_poly`, `_entity_poly_seq` and
  `_struct_conn` and groups the copies of one input entry into one entity, as Mol-1's does. DockQ v2 read no
  interface of the old atom_site-only file.
- **`tt-bio json`** turns PDB and mmCIF structures into Protenix / Mol-1 job JSON with Mol-1's own converter
  (`mol json`), so the output is identical to upstream's. `--altloc` picks the alternate location, `--assembly_id`
  expands to a biological assembly and `--include_discont_poly_poly_bonds` keeps bonds between non-consecutive polymer
  residues (disulfides, cyclic peptides), as upstream's options of the same names do. The first run downloads the
  Chemical Component Dictionary.
- **`tt-bio prep`** searches the MSAs of a Protenix / Mol-1 job JSON or a FASTA ahead of the fold and writes them
  where upstream's `mol msa` does, so a prepared job folds without searching. With `--use_template` and
  `--use_rna_msa` it also runs upstream's template and RNA MSA searches, which is `mol prep`. Needs no device.
- **Failed inputs get a report.** Every input `predict` could not fold or refused now leaves `ERR/<name>.txt` beside
  `results.json` with the reason, as Protenix and Mol-1 do. The exit status is unchanged.
- **`--checkpoint` works for Protenix-v1, Protenix-v2 and Mol-1**, and the shipped checkpoint it replaces is no longer
  downloaded (OpenFold3 and OpenBind-0 too).

### Fixed
- `tt-bio predict --use_template` on Protenix/Mol-1 job JSON refuses up front when `.a3m`/`.hhr` template hits
  need `kalign` and none is on PATH, instead of failing each job once a worker reaches it.
- Mol-1 accepts every ligand and modification CCD code in its own Chemical Component Dictionary. A code newer than
  the shared CCD library (A1A5U, YKX, A1EKL and about 6,100 others) used to be refused as unknown; upstream folds it.
  Mol-1's CCD table is rebuilt once on the next run (its pickle downloads again, 150 MB). Other models are unchanged.
- `tt-bio preflight mol1` no longer reports Mol-1 ready on a machine without the CCD molecule library it folds with.

### Changed
- **RoseTTAFold3 featurizes faster, with identical features.** Reference conformers come from
  worker processes that stay up between inputs, and each residue type is converted once instead of once per residue.
  A 512-residue RF3 input featurizes in 1.32 s instead of 1.96 s on a Wormhole Galaxy host, which comes straight off
  every fold on Wormhole and Blackhole.
- **ESMFold2 on Blackhole runs the MSA outer product's output projection on the shared pair-projection path.** A
  748-residue fold with a deep MSA on a p150a drops about 0.7 s in both modes (36.04 -> 35.36 s normal, 34.09 -> 33.36 s
  --fast), and the 512-residue page fold about 0.3 s. Graded over 44 paired folds per mode: normal CA-lDDT -0.0005
  [-0.0042, +0.0037], --fast +0.0024 [+0.0001, +0.0057]. Wormhole is unchanged.
- **ESMFold2 and ESMFold2-Fast send a smaller language-model dropout mask for lengths off the 16-residue grid.** The
  mask now crosses to the device bit-packed at every length (at 748 residues 18 MB a loop instead of 286 MB). A
  748-residue fold on a Blackhole p150a drops about 0.5 s (ESMFold2 normal 0.47 s, ESMFold2-Fast normal 0.57 s).
  Off-grid lengths draw a different dropout mask, so their structures change at the seed level: graded over 44 paired
  folds in normal mode, accuracy and docking success unchanged. Lengths on the grid are unchanged.
- **ESMFold2 folds with deep MSAs run faster.** When the MSA is deeper than 1024 rows, ESMFold2 re-encodes it every
  recycle, and those encoder transitions now run on the same fused kernel as the trunk's. A 748-residue complex with a
  4096-row MSA drops about 7 s on Blackhole `--fast` (40.9 -> 33.9 s); a 512-residue fold with the same MSA drops about
  3.5 s on a Wormhole chip, normal mode (36.9 -> 33.3 s), and 2.9 s with `--fast`. Blackhole normal mode is unchanged.
- **ESMFold2 and ESMFold2-Fast normal mode on Wormhole build the pair representation on the device.** A 512-residue
  fold drops about 1 s (ESMFold2 24.6 -> 23.5 s, ESMFold2-Fast 14.7 -> 13.7 s); `--fast` already did this.
  Structures stay within the accuracy bar for both changes.

### Added
- **`tt-bio predict jobs.json --use_template` and `--use_rna_msa` search what the JSON leaves out, as Mol-1 does.** A
  protein chain with an MSA directory but no `templatesPath` gets hmmsearch hits against the PDB seqres database, an RNA
  chain without `unpairedMsaPath` an nhmmer MSA. The binaries and databases take upstream's option names.
- **`--model mol1` writes the C-terminal O/OXT the way Mol-1 does**: the oxygen nearer C stays, OXT becomes its mirror
  across the C-CA axis. Other models keep the gated OpenDDE rebuild.
_releases.name: v0.27.0

**omicverse 2.4.0** — https://pypi.org/project/omicverse/2.4.0/  ·  `pip install -U omicverse`

42 commits since 2.3.2 — a multithreaded C++ backend becomes the default, plus new single-cell, spatial, bulk and imaging features and a round of performance work.

### Multithreaded C++ backend (`backend='cpp'`, default)
- **`backend=` / `ov.settings.backend`** on `qc`, `normalize_total`, `highly_variable_genes`, `preprocess`, `scale`, `pca`, `neighbors`, `umap`, `leiden`, `cosg`, `find_markers`, powered by [anndataoom-fast](https://pypi.org/project/anndataoom-fast/); `backend='python'` keeps the previous code; results independent of the thread count (#1022)
- In memory and out of core: SEA-AD MTG (1.38M cells, 32 threads) standard workflow in 1.5 min with 13 GB peak memory
- **Leiden** — brisc-style C++ Leiden by default under `cpp` (`flavor='leidenalg_exact'` for an exact leidenalg port); resolution lists in every mode (#1022, #1027)
- **UMAP** — deterministic multithreaded layout; new `ov.pp.localmap` / `ov.pp.pacmap`
- `find_markers(method='cosg')` streams from disk for AnnDataOOM (142 s / 105 GB → 2.1 s / 2.1 GB)

### GPU mode
- Works with rapids-singlecell 0.11–0.18; `neighbors(method=...)` no longer passed as the kNN algorithm (#1028)

### Performance
- pseudobulk up to 8.6x (#1026); AUCell 2.4x (#1025); `co_occurrence` memory 622 MB → 3.4 MB (#1024); scTenifoldKnk 24% (#1023)

### Features
- Single-cell: CellChat in PyTorch (`run_cellchat`); unified `run_ccc` (7 methods); dynamo perturbation backend; Scissor
- Spatial: pluggable segmentation backends + seam-free tiling (#1001); `match_cells` / `register_images` (#999); marker-panel annotation (#1004)
- Bulk & other: spike-in quantitative ChIP (#1021); `multisite_harmonize` (#1003); tumour/normal SNP-panel QC (#1020); pharmacophore-constrained docking (#1018); `fit_choice_model` (#1006); electrophysiology QC/ERP (#1002); radial cell annotation tree (#1019); ambient `method='envelope'` (#996)
- pyedger from PyPI instead of a vendored copy (#986)

### Fixes
- ARPACK int32 overflow in UMAP spectral init at ~1.66M–2M cells (#990); TMM before voom in limma paths (#995); PCA no longer fits twice

Full notes: https://github.com/omicverse/omicverse-tutorials/blob/main/docs/Release_notes.md

_releases.body:
### Fixed

- Every digest function now drops the parent's charge and its labile and unlocalised modifications from each product instead of copying them onto every peptide, which gave every product the wrong mass. A digestion product is a different molecule from the sequence it was cut out of: it does not carry the parent's charge, and neither a labile nor an unlocalised modification names the residue it sits on, so neither can be asserted of any one product. `pt.digest("PEPTIDEKTIDER/2", "trypsin")` returned `PEPTIDEK/2` and `TIDER/2`, each 2.014553 Da heavy by the parent's two protons, and `pt.digest("{Glycan:Hex}PEPTIDEKTIDER", "trypsin")` put the one Hex on both products, counting 162.0528 Da twice. Isotope labels and static modification rules are still copied, because a global label applies to every residue and a static rule applies to whichever products carry the residue it targets. This covers `digest`, `simple_digest`, `semi_digest`, `left_semi_digest`, `right_semi_digest` and `nonspecific_digest`. `ProFormaAnnotation.slice` is unchanged: slicing an annotation is not digesting it. That makes one previously true equality false, which is a visible change in what `digest` returns: for a parent carrying a charge, a labile modification or an unlocalised modification, a digest product is no longer the same string as the matching `annot[span].serialize()`, and it differs by exactly those three things. A test in this repository asserted that equality, so anyone who built on it was building on the wrong product masses this entry fixes.
- `estimate_isotopic_distribution` is importable from `peptacular.sequence`, which is where `docs/migration.rst` says the sequence-based estimate lives. It was listed in `peptacular.sequence.isotope.__all__` but left out of the package namespace, so only `ProFormaAnnotation.estimate_isotopic_distribution` or the submodule path reached it. The migration guide also read as though `pt.estimate_isotopic_distribution(annotations=...)` became `pt.estimate_isotopic_distribution(sequence=...)`. It never did: `pt.estimate_isotopic_distribution` takes a neutral mass in 4.x and 5.0 alike, and that row now names the paths that exist.

### Changed

- Optional-dependency floors are now the lowest release that actually passes the tests exercising them on Python 3.12, measured version by version instead of inherited. `mcp>=2.1.1,<2.4` becomes `mcp>=2.0.0,<3`: 2.0.0 is the first release with `mcp.server.MCPServer` (1.30.0 raises `ImportError`), and the old `<2.4` capped a version that has never been published. `pydantic>=2.13,<3` becomes `pydantic>=2.12,<3`, which is mcp's own minimum rather than ours. `alphabase>=1.9` becomes `alphabase>=1.0.3`: all 19 published releases below 1.0.3 install on Python 3.12 and all 19 fail the same terminal-modification round trip, leaving `Acetyl@Any_N-term` and `Amidated@Any_C-term` unregistered, and 1.0.3 is the first that passes. `psm-utils>=1.0` becomes `psm-utils>=0.9`: our surface is two API points and works back to 0.2.3, but 0.9 is the last pre-1.0 line and the oldest range we would actually fix. `numpy>=1.26` is unchanged and minimal, forced by cp312 wheel availability.
- `pyteomics>=5.0` is tightened to `pyteomics>=5.0.1`. Nothing was broken: pyteomics declares no unconditional dependencies at any version, and 5.0 declares exactly the same dependencies as 5.0.1, so 5.0 only reaches the interop path when `lxml` and `numpy` are already installed, which `peptacular[pyteomics]` does not provide. One resolution effect is worth naming: in the `interop` extra this floor resolves `psm-utils` 1.5.4 rather than 1.5.5, because `psm-utils` 1.5.5 caps `pyteomics<5` — by its own changelog a precaution against the next major release rather than a measured break. Nothing conflicts or fails, so the resolver takes the older `psm-utils` silently.
- The `alphabase` and `interop` extras now declare `pandas>=2.1.2`. The alphabase converters already imported pandas at run time without declaring it. 2.1.2 is the floor rather than 2.1.1, the first release with a cp312 wheel, because 2.1.1 requires `numpy>=1.26.0` with no upper bound: numpy 2.x then loads against a wheel built for the numpy 1.x C ABI and importing pandas raises `numpy.dtype size changed`. 2.1.2 added `numpy<2`, which sits inside our own `numpy>=1.26`. 2.2.2 is the first release to support the numpy 2 ABI.
_releases.name: v5.1.0

## Lobster AI 1.2.3

### `lobster serve` defaults and download checks
- `lobster serve` now listens on `127.0.0.1` by default. Serving on any other address requires a token: set `LOBSTER_SERVE_TOKEN` (preferred, because `--token` is visible in the process list) or pass `--token`. Clients send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. If a token is set, every request must send it, on localhost too.
- On a localhost bind, the server rejects requests whose `Host` or `Origin` is not a loopback address (`localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1`). Requests without an `Origin` header, such as from scripts, are accepted.
- `/query` and `/status` errors return a generic message instead of internal exception text.
- `lobster serve` speaks plain HTTP. For access from other machines, put it behind a TLS proxy or use an SSH tunnel.
- **Upgrade note:** Docker or remote setups that relied on the old `0.0.0.0` default must now pass `--host 0.0.0.0` (or another address) together with a token. `lobster serve` takes its address only from `--host`/`--port`; `HOST`/`PORT` in `.env` do not change it.
- GEO downloads and local archive loading refuse TAR archives that contain absolute paths, `..` paths, links pointing outside the extraction folder, or device files. Every member is checked before anything is extracted, so nothing from a refused archive is kept. A GEO series `RAW.tar` with such a member is refused as a whole; a nested per-sample archive with one is skipped with a warning, and the other samples still load.
- PRIDE, MassIVE, MetaboLights and GEO supplementary downloads keep only the base file name from remote listings and check that the result is inside the download folder; a name with nothing usable left is not downloaded. A cached download that is a symlink pointing outside the cache folder is no longer used.

### New
- **Ollama Cloud provider** (`ollama-cloud`, `OLLAMA_API_KEY`) for `init`, `chat`, `query` and `config`; `lobster init --ollama-cloud-key` for non-interactive setup.
- **Simplified Chinese** for the CLI and terminal UI: `--lang en|zh`, `LOBSTER_LANG`, or `/lang` in chat, which switches immediately. Command names, flags and JSON output stay in English.
- `lobster init` asks for the interface language first, unless `--lang` or `LOBSTER_LANG` already sets it.
- **`lobster upgrade`** upgrades `lobster-ai` in a `uv tool` install (keeping its extras) or in a virtual environment (with `uv pip` when `uv` is on PATH, otherwise `pip`). For other installs, such as system Python or conda, it prints the command to run instead. Editable development installs are not upgraded. `--dry-run` prints the command without running it.

### Fixes
- PRIDE, MassIVE and MetaboLights downloads no longer fail with `AttributeError: workspace_dir`.
- Exported notebook code for PRIDE and MassIVE downloads now creates the data manager correctly.
- Anthropic requests work again on fresh installs that resolve the Anthropic SDK 2.x.
- `lobster status` prints workspace paths that contain Rich markup literally.

### Changed
- `lobster init` uses the same workspace resolution as every other command (`LOBSTER_WORKSPACE`, else `./.lobster_workspace`). Re-running `init` without `--force` keeps an existing workspace configuration.
- Command output is quiet by default; `LOBSTER_LOG_LEVEL` or `--debug` restores diagnostic logs.
- `lobster init` no longer offers to install the npm client.
- The `HOST` setting and the `.env` templates generated by Lobster default to `127.0.0.1` and port `8000`, matching `lobster serve`'s defaults; `lobster serve` itself reads only `--host`/`--port`.
_releases.name: Lobster AI v1.2.3

* llm: an empty completion is no answer, not an AttributeError by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/242
* personal MCP links: document one URL per record; activation revokes too by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/243
* citations: take cited ids as a JSON list, not a comma string by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/247
* units: L/L is a volume fraction, 100 % of one by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/248
* docs: how a reading becomes comparable; the guides in Japanese by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/228
* fix(import): find the Apple Health export by its HealthData root by @mayuriphad in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/249
* frontend: sync the web client from mirobody-web 3b4bcfd by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/253
* frontend: sync the web client from mirobody-web 985f3c2 by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/254
* frontend: load the entry chunk the 985f3c2 sync renamed by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/255
* resolver: a name with 测定 or a flag after it codes like the bare name by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/252
* catalog: every series a decoder writes declares a daily statistic by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/250
* standardize: a LOINC code's name in Chinese for Chinese readers (#231) by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/256
* frontend: an MCP link for each record you can read by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/257
* apple: count an imported reading on its record's own day by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/260
* fix: prefer fresh Apple Health transport data for a day by @mvanhorn in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/261
* account merge: move a family member's MCP link to the kept account by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/258
* names: a plain name and what a test measures, in the reader's language (#231) by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/259
* observations: a name that folds to nothing is no name by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/251
* frontend: names for people, facets in the drawer, a dark palette by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/262
* contracts: stop naming two collect modules that no longer exist by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/263
* fix: preserve Apple daily figures during re-import recalculation by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/266
* release: 1.6.0 by @saltyfishtree in https://github.com/thetahealth/mirobody/pull/264
